findings.evidence: Reproduced 3/3: enter Full name X, Email invalid-email, select the first real category, Description short; click Submit request. Before clicking, name/email errors exist. The click adds the description error while focus remains #submit-request after 1000ms. No error summary or live region exists, no invalid field receives focus, and the title stays New service request. DOM mutation/focus traces and the Chromium accessibility tree are in evidence/client-invalid-notification.json. Keyboard Enter returns focus to Description; the empty-form path focuses Full name, so this is specific to the partially completed pointer path, not all submissions.
findings.userImpact: A screen reader user submitting through pointer or simulated-click interaction gets no programmatic status notification that the form was rejected and a new error appeared. Returning to each field is required to discover the problem.
findings.fix: Wire the client validator invalid-form/invalidHandler flow to the same accessible error-summary experience as the server path: populate field-linked text, update the error title, and reliably focus the summary after rejection. Alternatively announce the new errors through an appropriate pre-existing live region without moving focus. Keep stable aria-describedby IDs and aria-invalid behavior; regression-test the exact pointer path as well as keyboard, empty, and server paths.
findings.notes: This is not an axe violation. Field-to-error relationships are correct; the missing notification is a separate root cause from the previously fixed A11Y-003/004/005. No claim is made about a particular screen reader spoken output.

findings.evidence: At 320x640 the unmodified page has document width 320. With line-height 1.5, letter-spacing .12em, word-spacing .16em and paragraph margin-bottom 2em, the strong ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT token has a 338.84375px text range and document width is 339. Horizontal scrolling moves scrollX from 0 to 19. This is prose, not an exempt data table. See spacing-error-confirmed.json and spacing-error-default.png.
findings.userImpact: Users who enlarge text spacing on a narrow viewport must pan horizontally to read the environment-setting word.
findings.fix: Allow this long technical token to wrap, for example by marking it as code (the existing code selector uses overflow-wrap:anywhere), or applying equivalent wrapping to the relevant prose. Retest both normal and increased spacing at 320px; preserve the setting name.
findings.notes: Distinct from A11Y-008: the request ID code block still wraps correctly. No default-spacing reflow regression was observed.

findings.evidence: axe 4.10.3 reports aria-labelledby on the generic div as incomplete: naming is not well supported without a valid role. Chromium nevertheless exposes a focusable generic named There is a problem, focused=true, with a labelledby relation to the h2. All four summary links focus the correct fields. See axe-new-errors-server.json and summary-accessibility-tree.json.
findings.userImpact: The summary name is exposed in Chromium, but reliable announcement of a named generic container in other browser/assistive-technology combinations is not established.
findings.fix: Have an accessibility reviewer verify the focused summary with supported screen reader/browser combinations. If semantics need strengthening, give the summary an appropriate named region/group role and retest focus and linked errors. Do not treat axe incomplete as a confirmed violation.
findings.notes: Review candidate, excluded from score and blocking count. Prior Chromium evidence is reconfirmed, not contradicted.
